record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Asymptotic Geometric Analysis
record.context_brief: hyperplane conjecture for centered convex bodies
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0, independent of the dimension n, such that every centered convex body K in R^n with volume |K| = 1 has at least one hyperplane section through the origin whose (n-1)-dimensional volume is greater than c?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact convex set with nonempty interior. It is called centered if its centroid (barycenter) is the origin. For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $|K|$ denote its $n$-dimensional Lebesgue volume, and for a hyperplane $H\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ through the origin let $|K\cap H|$ denote the $(n-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue volume of the section $K\cap H$.

Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$, independent of the dimension $n$, with the following property: for every $n\ge 1$ and every centered convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $|K|=1$, there exists a hyperplane $H$ through the origin such that
$$|K\cap H| > c\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Bourgain's hyperplane (slicing) conjecture was resolved affirmatively in December 2024 by Boaz Klartag and Joseph Lehec, using a recent bound of Qingyang Guan together with stochastic localization, Milman's M-ellipsoid theory, and stability estimates for the Shannon–Stam inequality. The result has appeared in Geometric and Functional Analysis.

status_evidence.title: Affirmative Resolution of Bourgain's Slicing Problem using Guan's Bound
status_evidence.snippet: For any convex body K in R^n of volume one, there exists a hyperplane H such that the (n-1)-dimensional volume of K∩H is greater than a universal constant.
status_evidence.claim: Bourgain's slicing/hyperplane conjecture is resolved affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Qingyang Guan, Joseph Lehec and Bo'az Klartag Solved The Slice Conjecture!
status_evidence.snippet: Announcement that the slicing conjecture has been solved in December 2024.
status_evidence.claim: Independent commentary confirming the conjecture was solved.
